title: Ember and Choir
premise: Edmund Winterbourne, a bone-carver who hears the dead, has spent years keeping the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in impossible things, believing his invisibility keeps him safe. When the old gods resume answering prayers, a dead girl's voice leads him to discover her soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain by the Guild's own master, Aldous Crane, who bargains with the gods to seize their returning power. Edmund must ally with a disgraced priestess and a god grown small and desperate to steal the soul back before the equinox seals the court's doors for a century. In the end, Edmund chooses justice over safety: he burns the ledgers, unmaking the Guild's claims, and carries the girl's soul home himself, accepting that belonging means being seen—and being accountable.
about_author: Paloma Okonkwo is a former archivist who writes fantasy about the people history files away rather than celebrates. She lives near a river she refuses to learn how to name, and insists the dead make better editors than the living.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He carves a memorial bone for a drowned child while transcribing the Guild's latest impossible sale, establishing his double life as craftsman and clerk of wonders. When the child's ghost speaks to him—unusual, since the dead rarely address him directly—he feels the first crack in his careful invisibility. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: What the Gods Forgot
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The dead girl, Maren, reveals her soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain, and Edmund traces the transaction to Guildmaster Aldous Crane's private ledger. Meanwhile, prayers across the city begin receiving answers for the first time in generations, and the streets fill with desperate hope and dangerous fervor. Emotional beat: reluctant awakening; the past will not stay filed.

chapters.title: A Priestess Without a God
chapters.summary: Sera's POV introduced. Sera, defrocked when her temple's god went silent decades ago, recognizes the signs of returning divinity and comes to the Guild seeking records. She and Edmund recognize each other as fellow keepers of abandoned things. Crane watches them both with pleasant, unreadable courtesy. Emotional beat: two lonely professionals finding an uneasy kinship.

chapters.title: The Price of Being Seen
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Crane confronts Edmund privately, revealing he has always known about his gift and offers him partnership in the new age of answered gods—if he surrenders Maren's file. Edmund refuses and realizes Crane will now hunt him. He flees with Sera into the city's bone-market underbelly. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of losing one's safe life.

chapters.title: The God in the Gutter
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. They find Vessel, an old god reduced to a beggar-shape after centuries of unanswered prayer, who knows the roads beneath the mountain but demands a terrible toll: a worshipper's true devotion, freely given. Sera must decide whether faith can be rebuilt on something so diminished. Emotional beat: grief for what belief cost, and its stubborn survival.

chapters.title: Descent by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Guided by Vessel, the three enter the mountain through a corpse-road only the dead remember. They pass courts of the buried dead who test travelers with their own regrets; Edmund's ledger-keeping past becomes both weapon and wound as he must account for every entry he ever made. Emotional beat: reckoning—the books we keep keep us.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. They reach the underground court, where souls are currency and the dead nobility barter in memory. Edmund poses as a Guild auditor to access the vaults while Sera distracts the court with a false liturgy. They find Maren's soul—but discover Crane arrived days ago and struck his own bargain with the court's queen. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into betrayal.

chapters.title: Crane's Kingdom
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Confrontation with Crane, who reveals his plan: to broker the old gods' return as commodities, selling worship itself, with Maren's soul as the keystone contract. He offers Edmund authorship of the new order instead of erasure. Edmund understands at last that Crane corrupted power not through malice but through bookkeeping—turning everything sacred into entries. Emotional beat: clarity and cold fury.

chapters.title: The Burning of Accounts
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV (climax). During the equinox sealing ceremony, Edmund steals Maren's soul and sets fire to the master ledger, voiding every contract including Crane's claim on the gods. The court convulses as debts dissolve; Vessel spends the last of his divinity holding the gates open. Crane is dragged down by his own creditors. Emotional beat: sacrifice, chaos, and fierce moral triumph.

chapters.title: Ember and Choir
chapters.summary: Alternating Edmund and Sera POV. Above ground, the world adjusts to gods who answer without price, and the Guild's survivors scatter. Edmund lays Maren's soul to rest in carved bone, hearing her sing once before silence. Sera begins rebuilding worship around Vessel's ember-small flame, and asks Edmund to stay—not as a clerk, but as family. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited; a quiet, earned peace.
